We have plans to continue to improve the dense gas modeling capability by: • Continue building data set of real world storage and transportation methods for specific chemicals that result in dense gas characteristics. New data could come from new field studies, real-world accidents, and methods used common storage and transportation methods. During storage and transportation, normal gases are often frozen, liquified, or pressurized, which creates dense gas characteristics where the molecular weight higher than air. • Develop new SQA tests using dense gas algorithm and integrate into the full EPIcode SQA test suite. • Tweak/improve the dense gas parameters to improve modeling results. • Compare against any new dense gas field studies that may occur in the future. 26 LLNL-TR-818768 Appendix A References ▪ Britter, R., “The ground level extent of a negatively buoyant plume in a turbulent boundary layer,” Atmospheric Environment, 14(7), 779-785, 1980. ▪ Goldwire, Jr., H.C., T.G.
